# PRD — Gmail Sync for the Personal CRM

## Problem

Keeping each contact's `## Mark's Email History` section current is a manual chore
done through Claude Cowork + the Gmail MCP connector. We want a small, repeatable
**code** tool that reads Mark's Gmail directly (via the official API) and keeps
those sections up to date, one contact at a time.

The tool is a **refresher**, not a discoverer: it updates files that already exist,
driven by the email addresses in each file's frontmatter.

## Owner & vocabulary

See [`CONTEXT.md`](../CONTEXT.md) for the glossary (Contact, Owner, Direction,
`last_searched`, `last_updated`, "Mark's Email History"). Key terms:

- **Owner** — the single authenticated mailbox `mark@felicisholdings.com`, which
  also sends-as `mark@agilepainrelief.com`. Owner addresses are a configurable
  list.
- **Contact** — one markdown file in `client/`, `friends/`, or `colleagues/`,
  possibly with multiple email addresses (`emails:` list) or one (`email:`).

## Non-goals

1. **No discovery.** The tool never creates new contact files or classifies
   strangers into folders. New contacts arrive by a separate path.
2. **No summaries (yet).** The `Summary:` line is written by a later, separate
   stage. See *Open question* — solving this **gates go-live**.
3. **Never touch `## Email History`.** That section is Heather's mbox data
   (client files only) and is left byte-for-byte verbatim (CLAUDE.md rule 9).
4. **`last_updated` is not a watermark.** The tool ignores it entirely.

## Design decisions (resolved)

- **Library:** official `googleapis` package, pinned, installed under the repo's
  `min-release-age=7` `.npmrc`.
- **Auth:** Desktop OAuth 2.0 client, manual loopback consent flow (built on
  `google.auth.OAuth2` directly — no `@google-cloud/local-auth`, so no keyfile on
  disk), `gmail.readonly` scope only. The **client id is a public constant** in
  `src/gmail-auth.ts`; the **client secret is never persisted** — it is read every
  run from `process.env.GMAIL_OAUTH_SECRET`, supplied by **1Password** at run time
  with no file involved, e.g.
  `env "$(op environment read <item-id>)" npm run gmail-login`.
  The secret stays in memory only.
  Only the **refresh token** is saved, to gitignored `.secrets/token.json` —
  useless on its own without the secret. (A Desktop-client secret is not truly
  confidential per Google, so storing it at rest would also be acceptable; we chose
  the 1Password path for zero-paste convenience with nothing at rest.)
- **Search per contact:** one combined query
  `after:{last_searched} (from:(a OR b …) OR to:(a OR b …) OR cc:(a OR b …))`
  across all frontmatter addresses; messages fetched `format: metadata`
  (headers only — no bodies until summaries).
- **Watermark:** `last_searched` frontmatter field. First run (absent
  `last_searched`) ignores `last_updated`; its lower bound is a **per-category
  first-run floor** (client/colleague = 3 years, friend = 10 years back from today)
  so an initial scan of a decades-deep mailbox is bounded. Incremental runs use
  `last_searched` instead. The tool writes `last_searched` after each run;
  authoritative thereafter.
- **Direction:** Owner sent it (Gmail **`SENT` label** — authoritative across all
  of the Owner's historical addresses, not a fixed owner-address list) → **To
  {category}**; else contact is sender → **From {category}**; else **CC'd**.
  `{category}` = client / friend / colleague, from the folder. Drafts are skipped.
- **Rate limits:** every Gmail call is wrapped in exponential backoff + jitter,
  retrying on `429`, `403 rateLimitExceeded`, and `500/503`.
- **Dedup:** by Gmail **message id**, recorded on each new entry. Legacy entries
  (no message id) fall back to best-effort `(date, subject, direction, thread)`.
- **New entry shape:**
  ```
  - **Subject:** …
    - Direction: From friend
    - Thread: <hex thread id>
    - Message: <hex message id>
    - Link: https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#all/<message id>?authuser=mark@felicisholdings.com
  ```
  (No `Summary:` line yet — added by the later summary stage.)

## Slices

### Slice 1 — Prove Gmail login (Wahoo)
Authenticate via the Desktop OAuth loopback flow and make one `users.getProfile`
call.
**Acceptance:** running the tool prints the Owner's email address and total
message count; a `token.json` is persisted so re-runs need no browser.

### Slice 2 — Incremental search, read-only dry-run
For an explicit **few** contacts passed as arguments, run the combined OR-query,
derive direction, dedup against existing entries, and **print** the proposed new
entries (date, subject, direction, thread, message id, link) plus the
`last_searched` that *would* be written. **Writes nothing.**

Test set (varied on purpose):
- `friends/blyth-don.md` — 5 addresses, populated, `friend`.
- `client/abou-ward-sabrina.md` — single address, populated, `client`.
- `client/chelynne-schram2.md` — known recent exchange (positive case that must
  surface new mail).

**Acceptance:** for each test contact the dry-run lists the correct new messages
with correct direction; chelynne surfaces her post-Feb-2026 exchange; already-known
messages are not re-proposed; nothing on disk changes.

### Slice 3 — Solve the summary problem  *(gate before any live write)*
Design and build how the `Summary:` line gets generated (e.g. Claude API over the
message body). Out of scope for Slices 1–2; **live writes do not begin until this
is solved.**

### Slice 4 — Merge & write (live)
Build the surgical, section-scoped writer:
- Parse frontmatter + `## Mark's Email History` only; splice merged (existing ∪ new,
  deduped, re-sorted newest→oldest, grouped by date) entries; leave everything from
  `## Email History` onward verbatim.
- **Malformed / unlocatable `## Mark's Email History` → skip the file and report
  it** for manual fixing. No auto-repair.

## Qwen3 Series Overview

Qwen3 is the current generation of Qwen models. The Qwen3 lineup includes dense and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models of various sizes, available in 0.6B, 1.7B, 4B, 8B, 14B, 32B and 30B-A3B, 235B-A22B. The six dense models—Qwen3-32B, Qwen3-14B, Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-1.7B, and Qwen3-0.6B—are open-weighted under the Apache 2.0 license.

## Thinking vs. Non-Thinking Mode

A key feature of Qwen3 is its dual-mode capability. Qwen3 uniquely supports seamless switching between thinking mode (for complex logical reasoning, math, and coding) and non-thinking mode (for efficient, general-purpose dialogue) within a single model, ensuring optimal performance across various scenarios.

You can control this behavior in two ways:
- **Hard switch:** A hard switch strictly disables the model's thinking behavior, aligning its functionality with the previous Qwen2.5-Instruct models. This is particularly useful in scenarios where disabling thinking is essential for enhancing efficiency. This is done by setting enable_thinking=False, in which case the model will not generate any think content and will not include a <think>...</think> block.
- **Soft switch:** A soft switch mechanism allows users to dynamically control the model's behavior when enable_thinking=True. Specifically, you can add /think and /no_think to user prompts or system messages to switch the model's thinking mode from turn to turn.

## The 8B and 14B Models

Both the [Qwen3-8B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-8B) and [Qwen3-14B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-14B) models are available on Hugging Face. Key specs for both include:
- Context Length: 32,768 natively and 131,072 tokens with YaRN.
- FP8-quantized model checkpoints are also provided, with names ending in -FP8 (e.g., Qwen3-14B-FP8).

## Efficiency Gains

According to a 2026 lineup guide, the efficiency improvements are notable: compared to Qwen 2.5, the 8B matches the previous 14B in benchmarks, and the 32B matches the previous 72B. This is corroborated by the official Qwen team, who note that Qwen3-1.7B/4B/8B/14B/32B-Base perform as well as Qwen2.5-3B/7B/14B/32B/72B-Base, respectively.

## Vision-Language (VL) Variants

There is also a multimodal Qwen3-VL series with dedicated Instruct and Thinking editions, such as [Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct) and [Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking). These are available in Dense and MoE architectures that scale from edge to cloud, with Instruct and reasoning‑enhanced Thinking editions for flexible, on‑demand deployment.

## Availability

All dense models are available on Hugging Face under the QwenLM organization and can be pulled directly via Ollama. For local use, applications such as Ollama, LMStudio, MLX-LM, llama.cpp, and KTransformers have also added support for Qwen3.

# PRD — Gmail Sync for the Personal CRM

## Problem

Keeping each contact's `## Mark's Email History` section current is a manual chore
done through Claude Cowork + the Gmail MCP connector. We want a small, repeatable
**code** tool that reads Mark's Gmail directly (via the official API) and keeps
those sections up to date, one contact at a time.

The tool is a **refresher**, not a discoverer: it updates files that already exist,
driven by the email addresses in each file's frontmatter.

## Owner & vocabulary

See [`CONTEXT.md`](../CONTEXT.md) for the glossary (Contact, Owner, Direction,
`last_searched`, `last_updated`, "Mark's Email History"). Key terms:

- **Owner** — the single authenticated mailbox `mark@felicisholdings.com`, which
  also sends-as `mark@agilepainrelief.com`. Owner addresses are a configurable
  list.
- **Contact** — one markdown file in `client/`, `friends/`, or `colleagues/`,
  possibly with multiple email addresses (`emails:` list) or one (`email:`).

## Non-goals

1. **No discovery.** The tool never creates new contact files or classifies
   strangers into folders. New contacts arrive by a separate path.
2. **No summaries (yet).** The `Summary:` line is written by a later, separate
   stage. See *Open question* — solving this **gates go-live**.
3. **Never touch `## Email History`.** That section is Heather's mbox data
   (client files only) and is left byte-for-byte verbatim (CLAUDE.md rule 9).
4. **`last_updated` is not a watermark.** The tool ignores it entirely.

## Design decisions (resolved)

- **Library:** official `googleapis` package, pinned, installed under the repo's
  `min-release-age=7` `.npmrc`.
- **Auth:** Desktop OAuth 2.0 client, manual loopback consent flow (built on
  `google.auth.OAuth2` directly — no `@google-cloud/local-auth`, so no keyfile on
  disk), `gmail.readonly` scope only. The **client id is a public constant** in
  `src/gmail-auth.ts`; the **client secret is never persisted** — it is read every
  run from `process.env.GMAIL_OAUTH_SECRET`, supplied by **1Password** at run time
  with no file involved, e.g.
  `env "$(op environment read <item-id>)" npm run gmail-login`.
  The secret stays in memory only.
  Only the **refresh token** is saved, to gitignored `.secrets/token.json` —
  useless on its own without the secret. (A Desktop-client secret is not truly
  confidential per Google, so storing it at rest would also be acceptable; we chose
  the 1Password path for zero-paste convenience with nothing at rest.)
- **Search per contact:** one combined query
  `after:{last_searched} (from:(a OR b …) OR to:(a OR b …) OR cc:(a OR b …))`
  across all frontmatter addresses; messages fetched `format: metadata`
  (headers only — no bodies until summaries).
- **Watermark:** `last_searched` frontmatter field. First run (absent
  `last_searched`) ignores `last_updated`; its lower bound is a **per-category
  first-run floor** (client/colleague = 3 years, friend = 10 years back from today)
  so an initial scan of a decades-deep mailbox is bounded. Incremental runs use
  `last_searched` instead. The tool writes `last_searched` after each run;
  authoritative thereafter.
- **Direction:** Owner sent it (Gmail **`SENT` label** — authoritative across all
  of the Owner's historical addresses, not a fixed owner-address list) → **To
  {category}**; else contact is sender → **From {category}**; else **CC'd**.
  `{category}` = client / friend / colleague, from the folder. Drafts are skipped.
- **Rate limits:** every Gmail call is wrapped in exponential backoff + jitter,
  retrying on `429`, `403 rateLimitExceeded`, and `500/503`.
- **Dedup:** by Gmail **message id**, recorded on each new entry. Legacy entries
  (no message id) fall back to best-effort `(date, subject, direction, thread)`.
- **New entry shape:**
  ```
  - **Subject:** …
    - Direction: From friend
    - Thread: <hex thread id>
    - Message: <hex message id>
    - Link: https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#all/<message id>?authuser=mark@felicisholdings.com
  ```
  (No `Summary:` line yet — added by the later summary stage.)

## Slices

### Slice 1 — Prove Gmail login (Wahoo)
Authenticate via the Desktop OAuth loopback flow and make one `users.getProfile`
call.
**Acceptance:** running the tool prints the Owner's email address and total
message count; a `token.json` is persisted so re-runs need no browser.

### Slice 2 — Incremental search, read-only dry-run
For an explicit **few** contacts passed as arguments, run the combined OR-query,
derive direction, dedup against existing entries, and **print** the proposed new
entries (date, subject, direction, thread, message id, link) plus the
`last_searched` that *would* be written. **Writes nothing.**

Test set (varied on purpose):
- `friends/blyth-don.md` — 5 addresses, populated, `friend`.
- `client/abou-ward-sabrina.md` — single address, populated, `client`.
- `client/chelynne-schram2.md` — known recent exchange (positive case that must
  surface new mail).

**Acceptance:** for each test contact the dry-run lists the correct new messages
with correct direction; chelynne surfaces her post-Feb-2026 exchange; already-known
messages are not re-proposed; nothing on disk changes.

### Slice 3 — Summaries via a local model  *(gate before any live write)*

Generate the `Summary:` line with a **local Ollama model** — email bodies never
leave the machine (privacy), free at any volume.

- **Model:** Ollama, config constant. Validate the pipeline on the already-present
  `llama3.2:3b`; target `qwen2.5:7b` for quality. Official `ollama` npm package.
- **Input:** fetch the message `format: raw` → `mailparser` `simpleParser` →
  `.text` → **strip the quoted chain** (truncate at first reply marker: `On … wrote:`,
  `>`, `-----Original Message-----`, `From: … Sent: …`) and signature → cap ~2000 chars.
- **Prompt:** one sentence, name-led, Mark's POV, direction-aware (Mark sent → lead
  "Mark"; contact sent → lead with their first name; no `first_name` → "the
  {category}"). Temperature ~0.2. CC'd handled best-effort (rare).
- **Output contract:** first non-empty line, strip `Summary:`/quotes, single
  sentence, cap ~200 chars, end with a period. Sanity-check; on failure one retry at
  temp 0, then **skip** (write no `Summary:` line — never a fabricated one).
- **Failure modes:** Ollama unreachable → **fail fast** with a clear message; bad
  output → skip; per-request timeout ~60 s.
- **Architecture:** a **separate pass** (`gmail-summarize`) is the production path —
  it scans files for entries **missing** a `Summary:` line, fetches those bodies, and
  fills them; "missing summary" is the resumable work queue. **Sequential** is fine
  even for a one-time day-long first run (no concurrency). Validate now via a
  `--summarize` flag on the `gmail-sync` dry-run (fetches `raw`, prints the generated
  `Summary:` in place); the flag is scaffolding, likely removed once the separate
  pass exists.

**Live writes do not begin until summaries are trusted.**

### Slice 4 — Merge & write (live)
Build the surgical, section-scoped writer:
- Parse frontmatter + `## Mark's Email History` only; splice merged (existing ∪ new,
  deduped, re-sorted newest→oldest, grouped by date) entries; leave everything from
  `## Email History` onward verbatim.
- **Malformed / unlocatable `## Mark's Email History` → skip the file and report
  it** for manual fixing. No auto-repair.
- Write `last_searched` (and `last_updated`) per file **immediately after** syncing
  it, so an aborted run is resumable.
- Invocation: **no arg → all** contacts in `client/`, `friends/`, `colleagues/`,
  processed in stable (alphabetical) order; optional explicit file args for
  targeted runs.
- **Known wrinkle — legacy dedup date-shift.** Cowork-written entries carry no
  `Message:` id, so they dedup on `(date, subject, direction, thread)`. Cowork used
  the sender-timezone Date header while the tool uses the UTC `internalDate`, so
  the same message can differ by a day and dedup misses → a live write could append
  a duplicate of an already-present entry. Only affects the one-time transition over
  Cowork-populated files (all tool-written entries carry `Message:` ids and dedup
  exactly thereafter). Decide the mitigation here before enabling live writes:
  accept-and-clean, ±1-day tolerance on the legacy key, or regenerate the section
  from the API for the window and re-attach existing summaries.

## Open question (go-live gate)

**How is the `Summary:` line generated?** Everything through Slice 2 is
independent of this. Slice 4 (live writes) must not ship until Slice 3 resolves it.

Everything's wired. Here's how to run the quality pass — two options:

**Option A — pull the target model and judge real quality (recommended):**
```
ollama pull qwen3.5:9b-mlx
env OLLAMA_MODEL=qwen3.5:9b-mlx "$(op environment read ko66mhzn54ipyinybf2ftfci3q)" \
  npm run gmail-sync -- --summarize client/chelynne-schram2.md client/abou-ward-sabrina.md friends/blyth-don.md
```
(`env` takes both assignments — the model and the injected secret — then the command. `think: false` is applied automatically since it's a qwen3 model.)

**Option B — instant look on the already-installed 3B (no download):**
```
env "$(op environment read ko66mhzn54ipyinybf2ftfci3q)" \
  npm run gmail-sync -- --summarize client/chelynne-schram2.md client/abou-ward-sabrina.md friends/blyth-don.md
```

Blyth (~20 fresh) will take a few minutes either way; chelynne/abou-ward are quick.

**What to judge:** do the `Summary:` lines read like your Cowork ones — correct perspective per direction, one factual sentence, no quoted-chain bleed? Compare `qwen3.5:9b-mlx` vs `llama3.2:3b` if you run both. If 9B is clearly better (it should be), we lock it as the model; if 3B is good enough, we save the memory. Either way, a good result here is the **last gate before Slice 4 (live writes)** — where we also settle the legacy-dedup date-shift.

Paste a handful of summaries and we'll assess.

# Test-Driven Development

## Philosophy

**Core principle**: Tests should verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details. Code can change entirely; tests shouldn't.

**Good tests** are integration-style: they exercise real code paths through public APIs. They describe _what_ the system does, not _how_ it does it. A good test reads like a specification - "user can checkout with valid cart" tells you exactly what capability exists. These tests survive refactors because they don't care about internal structure.

**Bad tests** are coupled to implementation. They mock internal collaborators, test private methods, or verify through external means (like querying a database directly instead of using the interface). The warning sign: your test breaks when you refactor, but behavior hasn't changed. If you rename an internal function and tests fail, those tests were testing implementation, not behavior.

See [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for mocking guidelines.

## Anti-Pattern: Horizontal Slices

**DO NOT write all tests first, then all implementation.** This is "horizontal slicing" - treating RED as "write all tests" and GREEN as "write all code."

This produces **crap tests**:

- Tests written in bulk test _imagined_ behavior, not _actual_ behavior
- You end up testing the _shape_ of things (data structures, function signatures) rather than user-facing behavior
- Tests become insensitive to real changes - they pass when behavior breaks, fail when behavior is fine
- You outrun your headlights, committing to test structure before understanding the implementation

**Correct approach**: Vertical slices via tracer bullets. One test → one implementation → repeat. Each test responds to what you learned from the previous cycle. Because you just wrote the code, you know exactly what behavior matters and how to verify it.

```
WRONG (horizontal):
  RED:   test1, test2, test3, test4, test5
  GREEN: impl1, impl2, impl3, impl4, impl5

RIGHT (vertical):
  RED→GREEN: test1→impl1
  RED→GREEN: test2→impl2
  RED→GREEN: test3→impl3
  ...
```

## Workflow

### 1. Planning

When exploring the codebase, read `CONTEXT.md` (if it exists) so that test names and interface vocabulary match the project's domain language, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.

Before writing any code:

- [ ] Confirm with user what interface changes are needed
- [ ] Confirm with user which behaviors to test (prioritize)
- [ ] Identify opportunities for deep modules (small interface, deep implementation) — run the `/codebase-design` skill for the vocabulary and the testability checks
- [ ] List the behaviors to test (not implementation steps)
- [ ] Get user approval on the plan

Ask: "What should the public interface look like? Which behaviors are most important to test?"

**You can't test everything.** Confirm with the user exactly which behaviors matter most. Focus testing effort on critical paths and complex logic, not every possible edge case.

### 2. Tracer Bullet

Write ONE test that confirms ONE thing about the system:

```
RED:   Write test for first behavior → test fails
GREEN: Write minimal code to pass → test passes
```

This is your tracer bullet - proves the path works end-to-end.

### 3. Incremental Loop

For each remaining behavior:

```
RED:   Write next test → fails
GREEN: Minimal code to pass → passes
```

Rules:

- One test at a time
- Only enough code to pass current test
- Don't anticipate future tests
- Keep tests focused on observable behavior

### 4. Refactor

After all tests pass, look for [refactor candidates](refactoring.md):

- [ ] Extract duplication
- [ ] Deepen modules (move complexity behind simple interfaces)
- [ ] Apply SOLID principles where natural
- [ ] Consider what new code reveals about existing code
- [ ] Run tests after each refactor step

**Never refactor while RED.** Get to GREEN first.

## Checklist Per Cycle

```
[ ] Test describes behavior, not implementation
[ ] Test uses public interface only
[ ] Test would survive internal refactor
[ ] Code is minimal for this test
[ ] No speculative features added
```

# PRD — Gmail Sync for the Personal CRM

## Problem

Keeping each contact's `## Mark's Email History` section current is a manual chore
done through Claude Cowork + the Gmail MCP connector. We want a small, repeatable
**code** tool that reads Mark's Gmail directly (via the official API) and keeps
those sections up to date, one contact at a time.

The tool is a **refresher**, not a discoverer: it updates files that already exist,
driven by the email addresses in each file's frontmatter.

## Owner & vocabulary

See [`CONTEXT.md`](../CONTEXT.md) for the glossary (Contact, Owner, Direction,
`last_searched`, `last_updated`, "Mark's Email History"). Key terms:

- **Owner** — the single authenticated mailbox `mark@felicisholdings.com`, which
  also sends-as `mark@agilepainrelief.com`. Owner addresses are a configurable
  list.
- **Contact** — one markdown file in `client/`, `friends/`, or `colleagues/`,
  possibly with multiple email addresses (`emails:` list) or one (`email:`).

## Non-goals

1. **No discovery.** The tool never creates new contact files or classifies
   strangers into folders. New contacts arrive by a separate path.
2. **No summaries (yet).** The `Summary:` line is written by a later, separate
   stage. See *Open question* — solving this **gates go-live**.
3. **Never touch `## Email History`.** That section is Heather's mbox data
   (client files only) and is left byte-for-byte verbatim (CLAUDE.md rule 9).
4. **`last_updated` is not a watermark.** The tool ignores it entirely.

## Design decisions (resolved)

- **Library:** official `googleapis` package, pinned, installed under the repo's
  `min-release-age=7` `.npmrc`.
- **Auth:** Desktop OAuth 2.0 client, manual loopback consent flow (built on
  `google.auth.OAuth2` directly — no `@google-cloud/local-auth`, so no keyfile on
  disk), `gmail.readonly` scope only. The **client id is a public constant** in
  `src/gmail-auth.ts`; the **client secret is never persisted** — it is read every
  run from `process.env.GMAIL_OAUTH_SECRET`, supplied by **1Password** at run time
  with no file involved, e.g.
  `env "$(op environment read <item-id>)" npm run gmail-login`.
  The secret stays in memory only.
  Only the **refresh token** is saved, to gitignored `.secrets/token.json` —
  useless on its own without the secret. (A Desktop-client secret is not truly
  confidential per Google, so storing it at rest would also be acceptable; we chose
  the 1Password path for zero-paste convenience with nothing at rest.)
- **Search per contact:** one combined query
  `after:{last_searched} (from:(a OR b …) OR to:(a OR b …) OR cc:(a OR b …))`
  across all frontmatter addresses; messages fetched `format: metadata`
  (headers only — no bodies until summaries).
- **Watermark:** `last_searched` frontmatter field. First run (absent
  `last_searched`) ignores `last_updated`; its lower bound is a **per-category
  first-run floor** (client/colleague = 3 years, friend = 10 years back from today)
  so an initial scan of a decades-deep mailbox is bounded. Incremental runs use
  `last_searched` instead. The tool writes `last_searched` after each run;
  authoritative thereafter.
- **Direction:** Owner sent it (Gmail **`SENT` label** — authoritative across all
  of the Owner's historical addresses, not a fixed owner-address list) → **To
  {category}**; else contact is sender → **From {category}**; else **CC'd**.
  `{category}` = client / friend / colleague, from the folder. Drafts are skipped.
- **Rate limits:** every Gmail call is wrapped in exponential backoff + jitter,
  retrying on `429`, `403 rateLimitExceeded`, and `500/503`.
- **Dedup:** by Gmail **message id**, recorded on each new entry. Legacy entries
  (no message id) fall back to best-effort `(date, subject, direction, thread)`.
- **New entry shape:**
  ```
  - **Subject:** …
    - Direction: From friend
    - Thread: <hex thread id>
    - Message: <hex message id>
    - Link: https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#all/<message id>?authuser=mark@felicisholdings.com
  ```
  (No `Summary:` line yet — added by the later summary stage.)

## Slices

### Slice 1 — Prove Gmail login (Wahoo)
Authenticate via the Desktop OAuth loopback flow and make one `users.getProfile`
call.
**Acceptance:** running the tool prints the Owner's email address and total
message count; a `token.json` is persisted so re-runs need no browser.

### Slice 2 — Incremental search, read-only dry-run
For an explicit **few** contacts passed as arguments, run the combined OR-query,
derive direction, dedup against existing entries, and **print** the proposed new
entries (date, subject, direction, thread, message id, link) plus the
`last_searched` that *would* be written. **Writes nothing.**

Test set (varied on purpose):
- `friends/blyth-don.md` — 5 addresses, populated, `friend`.
- `client/abou-ward-sabrina.md` — single address, populated, `client`.
- `client/chelynne-schram2.md` — known recent exchange (positive case that must
  surface new mail).

**Acceptance:** for each test contact the dry-run lists the correct new messages
with correct direction; chelynne surfaces her post-Feb-2026 exchange; already-known
messages are not re-proposed; nothing on disk changes.

### Slice 3 — Summaries via a local model  *(gate before any live write)*

Generate the `Summary:` line with a **local Ollama model** — email bodies never
leave the machine (privacy), free at any volume.

- **Model:** Ollama, config constant (`OLLAMA_MODEL` env). Validate the pipeline on
  the already-present `llama3.2:3b`; target **`qwen3.5:9b-mlx`** for quality (≤15B,
  MLX-fast on Apple Silicon, run **non-thinking** — auto `think: false` for any
  qwen3 model, override via `OLLAMA_THINK`). Official `ollama` npm package.
- **Input:** fetch the message `format: raw` → `mailparser` `simpleParser` →
  `.text` → **strip the quoted chain** (truncate at first reply marker: `On … wrote:`,
  `>`, `-----Original Message-----`, `From: … Sent: …`) and signature → cap ~2000 chars.
- **Prompt:** one sentence, name-led, Mark's POV, direction-aware (Mark sent → lead
  "Mark"; contact sent → lead with their first name; no `first_name` → "the
  {category}"). Temperature ~0.2. CC'd handled best-effort (rare).
- **Output contract:** first non-empty line, strip `Summary:`/quotes, single
  sentence, cap ~200 chars, end with a period. Sanity-check; on failure one retry at
  temp 0, then **skip** (write no `Summary:` line — never a fabricated one).
- **Failure modes:** Ollama unreachable → **fail fast** with a clear message; bad
  output → skip; per-request timeout ~60 s.
- **Architecture:** a **separate pass** (`gmail-summarize`) is the production path —
  it scans files for entries **missing** a `Summary:` line, fetches those bodies, and
  fills them; "missing summary" is the resumable work queue. **Sequential** is fine
  even for a one-time day-long first run (no concurrency). Validate now via a
  `--summarize` flag on the `gmail-sync` dry-run (fetches `raw`, prints the generated
  `Summary:` in place); the flag is scaffolding, likely removed once the separate
  pass exists.

**Live writes do not begin until summaries are trusted.**

### Slice 4 — Merge & write (live)
Build the surgical, section-scoped writer:
- Parse frontmatter + `## Mark's Email History` only; splice merged (existing ∪ new,
  deduped, re-sorted newest→oldest, grouped by date) entries; leave everything from
  `## Email History` onward verbatim.
- **Malformed / unlocatable `## Mark's Email History` → skip the file and report
  it** for manual fixing. No auto-repair.
- Write `last_searched` (and `last_updated`) per file **immediately after** syncing
  it, so an aborted run is resumable.
- Invocation: **no arg → all** contacts in `client/`, `friends/`, `colleagues/`,
  processed in stable (alphabetical) order; optional explicit file args for
  targeted runs.
- **Known wrinkle — legacy dedup date-shift.** Cowork-written entries carry no
  `Message:` id, so they dedup on `(date, subject, direction, thread)`. Cowork used
  the sender-timezone Date header while the tool uses the UTC `internalDate`, so
  the same message can differ by a day and dedup misses → a live write could append
  a duplicate of an already-present entry. Only affects the one-time transition over
  Cowork-populated files (all tool-written entries carry `Message:` ids and dedup
  exactly thereafter). Decide the mitigation here before enabling live writes:
  accept-and-clean, ±1-day tolerance on the legacy key, or regenerate the section
  from the API for the window and re-attach existing summaries.

## Open question (go-live gate)

**How is the `Summary:` line generated?** Everything through Slice 2 is
independent of this. Slice 4 (live writes) must not ship until Slice 3 resolves it.

## Slice 4 done — TDD, 8 vitest specs, all green

**`src/merge.ts`** (pure, fully unit-tested — no Gmail needed):
`mergeContact(existingContent, fetched, today)` → splices new entries into `## Mark's Email History`, dedups (Message id, else exact legacy 4-tuple), sorts newest-first grouped by date, advances `last_searched` always / `last_updated` only when something changed, preserves the placeholder when nothing's found, and leaves `## Email History` **byte-for-byte**. Missing heading → `skipped-malformed`, untouched.

**The 8 behaviors covered:** splice + mbox-verbatim · message-id dedup · legacy exact dedup · newest-first grouping · placeholder replacement · malformed-skip · frontmatter set-on-add · watermark-advance-but-preserve-placeholder-on-empty.

**`gmail-sync --write`** wires it in; dry-run stays the default. `no-arg → all` is deliberately **not** enabled yet, so you can't mass-write 315 files by accident.

# PRD — Gmail Sync for the Personal CRM

## Problem

Keeping each contact's `## Mark's Email History` section current is a manual chore
done through Claude Cowork + the Gmail MCP connector. We want a small, repeatable
**code** tool that reads Mark's Gmail directly (via the official API) and keeps
those sections up to date, one contact at a time.

The tool is a **refresher**, not a discoverer: it updates files that already exist,
driven by the email addresses in each file's frontmatter.

## Owner & vocabulary

See [`CONTEXT.md`](../CONTEXT.md) for the glossary (Contact, Owner, Direction,
`last_searched`, `last_updated`, "Mark's Email History"). Key terms:

- **Owner** — the single authenticated mailbox `mark@felicisholdings.com`, which
  also sends-as `mark@agilepainrelief.com`. Owner addresses are a configurable
  list.
- **Contact** — one markdown file in `client/`, `friends/`, or `colleagues/`,
  possibly with multiple email addresses (`emails:` list) or one (`email:`).

## Non-goals

1. **No discovery.** The tool never creates new contact files or classifies
   strangers into folders. New contacts arrive by a separate path.
2. **No summaries (yet).** The `Summary:` line is written by a later, separate
   stage. See *Open question* — solving this **gates go-live**.
3. **Never touch `## Email History`.** That section is Heather's mbox data
   (client files only) and is left byte-for-byte verbatim (CLAUDE.md rule 9).
4. **`last_updated` is not a watermark.** The tool ignores it entirely.

## Design decisions (resolved)

- **Library:** official `googleapis` package, pinned, installed under the repo's
  `min-release-age=7` `.npmrc`.
- **Auth:** Desktop OAuth 2.0 client, manual loopback consent flow (built on
  `google.auth.OAuth2` directly — no `@google-cloud/local-auth`, so no keyfile on
  disk), `gmail.readonly` scope only. The **client id is a public constant** in
  `src/gmail-auth.ts`; the **client secret is never persisted** — it is read every
  run from `process.env.GMAIL_OAUTH_SECRET`, supplied by **1Password** at run time
  with no file involved, e.g.
  `env "$(op environment read <item-id>)" npm run gmail-login`.
  The secret stays in memory only.
  Only the **refresh token** is saved, to gitignored `.secrets/token.json` —
  useless on its own without the secret. (A Desktop-client secret is not truly
  confidential per Google, so storing it at rest would also be acceptable; we chose
  the 1Password path for zero-paste convenience with nothing at rest.)
- **Search per contact:** one combined query
  `after:{last_searched} (from:(a OR b …) OR to:(a OR b …) OR cc:(a OR b …))`
  across all frontmatter addresses; messages fetched `format: metadata`
  (headers only — no bodies until summaries).
- **Watermark:** `last_searched` frontmatter field. First run (absent
  `last_searched`) ignores `last_updated`; its lower bound is a **per-category
  first-run floor** (client/colleague = 3 years, friend = 10 years back from today)
  so an initial scan of a decades-deep mailbox is bounded. Incremental runs use
  `last_searched` instead. The tool writes `last_searched` after each run;
  authoritative thereafter.
- **Direction:** Owner sent it (Gmail **`SENT` label** — authoritative across all
  of the Owner's historical addresses, not a fixed owner-address list) → **To
  {category}**; else contact is sender → **From {category}**; else **CC'd**.
  `{category}` = client / friend / colleague, from the folder. Drafts are skipped.
- **Rate limits:** every Gmail call is wrapped in exponential backoff + jitter,
  retrying on `429`, `403 rateLimitExceeded`, and `500/503`.
- **Dedup:** by Gmail **message id**, recorded on each new entry. Legacy entries
  (no message id) fall back to best-effort `(date, subject, direction, thread)`.
- **New entry shape:**
  ```
  - **Subject:** …
    - Direction: From friend
    - Thread: <hex thread id>
    - Message: <hex message id>
    - Link: https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#all/<message id>?authuser=mark@felicisholdings.com
  ```
  (No `Summary:` line yet — added by the later summary stage.)

## Slices

### Slice 1 — Prove Gmail login (Wahoo)
Authenticate via the Desktop OAuth loopback flow and make one `users.getProfile`
call.
**Acceptance:** running the tool prints the Owner's email address and total
message count; a `token.json` is persisted so re-runs need no browser.

### Slice 2 — Incremental search, read-only dry-run
For an explicit **few** contacts passed as arguments, run the combined OR-query,
derive direction, dedup against existing entries, and **print** the proposed new
entries (date, subject, direction, thread, message id, link) plus the
`last_searched` that *would* be written. **Writes nothing.**

Test set (varied on purpose):
- `friends/blyth-don.md` — 5 addresses, populated, `friend`.
- `client/abou-ward-sabrina.md` — single address, populated, `client`.
- `client/chelynne-schram2.md` — known recent exchange (positive case that must
  surface new mail).

**Acceptance:** for each test contact the dry-run lists the correct new messages
with correct direction; chelynne surfaces her post-Feb-2026 exchange; already-known
messages are not re-proposed; nothing on disk changes.

### Slice 3 — Summaries via a local model  *(gate before any live write)*

Generate the `Summary:` line with a **local Ollama model** — email bodies never
leave the machine (privacy), free at any volume.

- **Model:** Ollama, config constant (`OLLAMA_MODEL` env). Validate the pipeline on
  the already-present `llama3.2:3b`; target **`qwen3.5:9b-mlx`** for quality (≤15B,
  MLX-fast on Apple Silicon, run **non-thinking** — auto `think: false` for any
  qwen3 model, override via `OLLAMA_THINK`). Official `ollama` npm package.
- **Input:** fetch the message `format: raw` → `mailparser` `simpleParser` →
  `.text` → **strip the quoted chain** (truncate at first reply marker: `On … wrote:`,
  `>`, `-----Original Message-----`, `From: … Sent: …`) and signature → cap ~2000 chars.
- **Prompt:** one sentence, name-led, Mark's POV, direction-aware (Mark sent → lead
  "Mark"; contact sent → lead with their first name; no `first_name` → "the
  {category}"). Temperature ~0.2. CC'd handled best-effort (rare).
- **Output contract:** first non-empty line, strip `Summary:`/quotes, single
  sentence, cap ~200 chars, end with a period. Sanity-check; on failure one retry at
  temp 0, then **skip** (write no `Summary:` line — never a fabricated one).
- **Failure modes:** Ollama unreachable → **fail fast** with a clear message; bad
  output → skip; per-request timeout ~60 s.
- **Architecture:** a **separate pass** (`gmail-summarize`) is the production path —
  it scans files for entries **missing** a `Summary:` line, fetches those bodies, and
  fills them; "missing summary" is the resumable work queue. **Sequential** is fine
  even for a one-time day-long first run (no concurrency). Validate now via a
  `--summarize` flag on the `gmail-sync` dry-run (fetches `raw`, prints the generated
  `Summary:` in place); the flag is scaffolding, likely removed once the separate
  pass exists.

**Live writes do not begin until summaries are trusted.**

### Slice 4 — Merge & write (live)  *(implemented, TDD with vitest)*

`src/merge.ts` — pure `mergeContact(existingContent, fetched, today)`, 8 vitest specs
in `src/merge.test.ts`. Wired into `gmail-sync` behind **`--write`** (dry-run stays
default). **Dedup = exact only** (Message id, else legacy `(date,subject,direction,
thread)`) — a looser key risks silently dropping a real message, so the one-time
transition may show a few duplicates on Cowork-populated files (delete by hand).
**`no-arg → all` is deferred** — explicit file args still required, so a 315-contact
mass write can't happen by accident; git diff is the safety net for the test phase.

Build the surgical, section-scoped writer:
- Parse frontmatter + `## Mark's Email History` only; splice merged (existing ∪ new,
  deduped, re-sorted newest→oldest, grouped by date) entries; leave everything from
  `## Email History` onward verbatim.
- **Malformed / unlocatable `## Mark's Email History` → skip the file and report
  it** for manual fixing. No auto-repair.
- Write `last_searched` (and `last_updated`) per file **immediately after** syncing
  it, so an aborted run is resumable.
- Invocation: **no arg → all** contacts in `client/`, `friends/`, `colleagues/`,
  processed in stable (alphabetical) order; optional explicit file args for
  targeted runs.
- **Known wrinkle — legacy dedup date-shift.** Cowork-written entries carry no
  `Message:` id, so they dedup on `(date, subject, direction, thread)`. Cowork used
  the sender-timezone Date header while the tool uses the UTC `internalDate`, so
  the same message can differ by a day and dedup misses → a live write could append
  a duplicate of an already-present entry. Only affects the one-time transition over
  Cowork-populated files (all tool-written entries carry `Message:` ids and dedup
  exactly thereafter). Decide the mitigation here before enabling live writes:
  accept-and-clean, ±1-day tolerance on the legacy key, or regenerate the section
  from the API for the window and re-attach existing summaries.

## Open question (go-live gate)

**How is the `Summary:` line generated?** Everything through Slice 2 is
independent of this. Slice 4 (live writes) must not ship until Slice 3 resolves it.

## Problem

Keeping each contact's `## Mark's Email History` section current is a manual chore
done through Claude Cowork + the Gmail MCP connector. We want a small, repeatable
**code** tool that reads Mark's Gmail directly (via the official API) and keeps
those sections up to date, one contact at a time.
